tables.10: Hazardous — fire, HV exposure, or injury risk.
tables.3: Minor — small maintenance delay, no performance loss.
tables.4: Low — minor performance loss, car still finishes.
tables.5: Moderate — noticeable derate or repair between runs.
tables.6: Significant — thermal derate / partial loss of function in event.
tables.7: High — likely DNF or failed scrutineering check.
tables.8: Very high — DNF plus damage to an expensive component.
tables.9: Serious — rule violation or potential safety hazard.

tables.1: Remote — strong prevention control + prior proof it doesn't happen.
tables.10: Near-certain — failure is essentially guaranteed as drawn.
tables.2: Very low — robust design margin, documented.
tables.3: Low — good design practice, some supporting analysis.
tables.4: Low-moderate — reasonable design, no hard proof yet.
tables.5: Moderate — plausible cause, control exists but unproven.
tables.6: Moderate-high — similar parts have failed before.
tables.8: Very high — known marginal area, no prevention control.
tables.9: Frequent — expected to occur without a design change.

tables.1: Almost certain — reliable test/inspection before every run.
tables.10: None — no possible detection before the car runs.
tables.2: Very high — strong documented check before use.
tables.3: High — specific test or FEA/CFD catches it.
tables.4: Moderately high — inspection likely catches it.
tables.5: Moderate — generic check, may catch it.
tables.6: Low-moderate — only caught if someone looks carefully.
tables.7: Low — no dedicated check, relies on luck.
tables.8: Very low — hard to detect before failure.
tables.9: Remote — essentially only found after it fails on track.
